items.title: Rethinking Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction in Hypertension: The Interplay of Arterial Stiffness, Ventricular-Arterial Coupling, and Pulse Wave Velocity in HFpEF.
items.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for approximately half of heart failure cases and is closely associated with hypertension and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD). This narrative review examines the relationship between diastolic function, arterial stiffness, and ventricular-arterial coupling in hypertensive heart disease. We summarize ventricular relaxation and filling and discuss echocardiographic measures, including E/e', left atrial volume, and left atrial reservoir strain, for assessing diastolic function and filling pressures. We then examine how aortic stiffening may increase late systolic load and contribute to ventricular remodeling and impaired relaxation. This review addresses four central questions: whether arterial stiffness represents an independent component of hypertensive left ventricular diastolic dysfunction; whether pulse wave velocity (PWV) is primarily a marker of vascular aging, ventricular afterload, or HFpEF risk; whether PWV provides incremental information beyond established echocardiographic markers; and how arterial stiffness could be integrated into contemporary HFpEF assessment. The available evidence supports arterial stiffness as a biologically plausible contributor to hypertensive ventricular remodeling and impaired diastolic reserve. However, current evidence does not establish echocardiographic global PWV (PWVg) as an independent diagnostic criterion or validated prognostic marker of clinical HFpEF. We therefore propose PWVg as a complementary, hypothesis-generating measure for vascular and ventricular phenotyping, to be interpreted alongside clinical assessment, natriuretic peptides, multiparametric echocardiography, and exercise or invasive hemodynamic testing when indicated.

items.title: gutDBase: a comprehensive database for uncovering heterogeneous molecular characteristics of 15 gut-related diseases.
items.abstract: The gut plays key roles in digestion, nutrient absorption, and immunity. A variety of gut-related diseases have shown great heterogeneity in many aspects, including molecular characteristics, cellular composition, and microbial communities, which may reveal disease-specific therapeutic targets. In recent years, large-scale datasets have emerged to decipher associations between gut-related diseases and characteristics. However, these valuable data are independently scattered in different studies, and no comprehensive resource is available for integrating these data, which limits systematic investigation and cross-disease comparisons. To address this, we developed gutDBase (https://bio-computing.hrbmu.edu.cn/gutDBase), a comprehensive database that systematically integrates transcriptomic and microbial data for 15 gut-related diseases, curated from 175 bulk and single-cell datasets derived from 161 publications. gutDBase provides a user-friendly, interactive interface, and rich visualization tools to display the expression patterns and microbial compositions of different diseases from multiple perspectives. This resource is intended to support studies of disease mechanisms, facilitate target discovery, and advance translational research in gut-related diseases.

items.title: Development and validation of early warning scores predicting 24 h mortality addressing intercurrent medical interventions in Denmark: a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 2·08 million hospital encounters.
items.abstract: The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is widely used to predict patient deterioration, but retrospective validations face intervention bias and emphasise discrimination performance over clinical utility. We aimed to compare the clinical net benefit of NEWS against simplified scoring rules and machine learning models, to determine whether simpler approaches suffice or if complex models offer meaningful advantages, and to evaluate performance heterogeneity across patient subgroups. In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, we included data from 15 Danish hospitals (ten hospital networks) across the Capital and Zealand regions of Denmark, between Oct 16, 2018, and Oct 16, 2023. We included all adults (aged ≥18 years) with a hospital encounter with at least one NEWS assessment. Demographic and clinical data, NEWS data, and time of death were extracted from hospital and regional electronic health records. Patients were followed up until death or completion of the 24 h observation period after the initial NEWS score was recorded, whichever occurred first. The outcome was all-cause mortality within 24 h of the initial NEWS recording. We compared NEWS against both simpler and more complex approaches for predicting 24 h mortality: simplified NEWS (NEWS without blood pressure and temperature), Demographic Early Warning Score (DEWS; simplified NEWS with age and sex), and a model based on Extreme Gradient Boosting Early Warning Score (XGB-EWS) incorporating vital signs, demographics, laboratory markers, plus medical history embeddings extracted using sentence transformers. We used propensity score weighting to mitigate intervention bias and evaluated performance using net benefit, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and calibration. This study included data for 2 080 765 hospital encounters representing 825 200 unique patients over 5 years. The majority (50·9%) of the weighted population was aged 18-65 years, 50·4% were female, 49·6% were male, and 66·2% were admitted to internal and acute medicine clinical specialties. Decision curve analysis in the overall population showed maximum net benefit differences of 1·9 additional correct mortality identifications per 10 000 patients between XGB-EWS and NEWS, and 1·5 per 10 000 patients between NEWS and simplified NEWS. However, stratified analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: in the high-risk group (initial NEWS ≥7), XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 78·1 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, whereas simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum performance loss of 60·2 per 10 000 patients. Conversely, in the low-risk group (NEWS 0-4), differences were minimal: XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 0·9 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, while simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum loss of 0·1 per 10 000 patients. Model complexity produced small average clinical utility gains, concentrated among patients initially classified as high risk by NEWS. These findings support prospective trials of risk-stratified monitoring based on the first NEWS assessment, testing simplified approaches for lower-risk patients while retaining full NEWS or electronic health record models for higher-risk patients. items.title: What's Hot in Coronary Artery Disease? Innovation With Consideration of Scale and Equity.
Implementation of an Accelerated Treatment Pathway for Patients with Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
items.abstract: Contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy for patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) includes four classes of drugs with independent and additive benefits. While current guidelines recommend early initiation and rapid dose titration of quadruple therapy, its effective and safe implementation in real-world clinical practice remains uncertain. A nurse-led clinical pathway was developed to support early in-hospital initiation of quadruple therapy and rapid post-discharge titration for patients admitted with HFrEF. The Accelerated Treatment (ACT) Pathway was introduced for patients admitted under the Cardiology Service at Te Toka Tumai Auckland Hospital, New Zealand. The pathway involves initiating low-dose quadruple therapy before discharge, followed by weekly clinic visits to facilitate individualised drug up-titration over a 4-week period. Follow-up echocardiography was performed after 3 months to re-assess left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) according to usual clinical practice. This report describes the early experience with the ACT Pathway, including drug use, safety outcomes, and changes in LVEF in response to treatment. Between March 2023 and October 2024, 103 patients proceeded with the planned pathway. The mean age was 57 years, 20% were women, 67% were non-New Zealand European (including 17% Māori and 27% Pacific), 59% had non-ischaemic heart failure, and the median LVEF was 27%. At hospital discharge, quadruple therapy was successfully initiated, with all patients receiving renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors, 96% beta blockers, 87% spironolactone, and 55% sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors. The proportion of patients meeting the performance measure (≥50% of the maximum dosage) increased from discharge to 4 weeks as follows: RAAS inhibitors, 31%-82%; and beta blockers, 35%-69% (all p<0.001); and the proportion of patients receiving mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists increased from 87% to 92%. Loop diuretic use decreased: only 40% of patients were still receiving a daily dose of diuretic at 4 weeks. There were no hospital admissions due to hypotension or acute kidney injury. Median LVEF was 27% (interquartile range [IQR] 20-33) during hospitalisation and 43% (IQR 34-50) after 3 months, an overall increase of 13 percentage points (p<0.001). The implementation of the ACT Pathway successfully achieved its goal of safe, early initiation and rapid titration of quadruple therapy to maximum tolerated doses within 4 weeks in patients admitted with HFrEF in a real-world setting. This pathway has demonstrated the potential for substantial benefits for patients, whānau, and the health care system in a New Zealand context.

items.title: AI-Driven Structural Analysis Clarifies Novel TNFRSF17 Variants of Uncertain Significance as Candidate Resistance Mechanisms to BCMA-Targeted Immunotherapies in Multiple Myeloma.
items.abstract: B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed immunotherapies have transformed care of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (r/r MM), but most patients eventually progress. When whole-genome sequencing (WGS) at relapse reveals variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in the BCMA gene TNFRSF17, their functional significance and relevance to subsequent BCMA-directed therapy remain uncertain. We developed a structure-based framework to generate agent-level hypotheses of therapeutic binding after BCMA-directed therapy. We analyzed a cohort of patients with r/r MM who underwent routine WGS at progression after BCMA-directed therapy at 2 German tertiary cancer centers; among the 25 evaluable samples, four non-truncating TNFRSF17 VUS were identified. These VUS were analyzed using a structure-informed framework to generate agent-specific predictions of preserved versus impaired therapeutic binding. Incremental discrimination was explored by comparison with direct disulfide-cysteine and agent-contact-only rules on experimentally labeled mutation-agent pairs. The framework identified three predicted structural and binding patterns. Variants directly affecting the C24-C37 or C28-C41 disulfide bonds showed the broadest predicted extracellular-domain and therapeutic-interface perturbation. The non-cysteine P23delins9 variant was also predicted to cause substantial backbone and interface remodeling, whereas C8-C21 disulfide-bond alterations and non-cysteine epitope variants showed agent-dependent predicted binding effects. In the two index patients, predictions for the therapies received were directionally concordant with progression. Structural interpretation of TNFRSF17 variants may help prioritize newly identified variants for agent-specific functional evaluation. Direct disulfide-cysteine alterations were associated with broader predicted structural perturbation, non-cysteine variants more often showed agent-dependent effects. Prospective functional and clinical validation is required.

items.title: Real-World Treatment and Outcomes for Patients With Deficient Mismatch Repair Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Following Pembrolizumab Availability in Australia.
items.abstract: The 5-year follow-up results of KEYNOTE-177 established pembrolizumab as a standard first-line (1L) treatment for deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), demonstrating improved response rates, progression-free survival (PFS), and tolerability over chemotherapy. Pembrolizumab became available as a 1L option in Australia following government reimbursement in August 2021. Real-world treatment patterns and outcomes in Australia since then have not previously been reported. Patients with dMMR mCRC diagnosed from August 1, 2021 to May 30, 2025, were analyzed using data from Treatment of Recurrent and Advanced Colorectal Cancer (TRACC) and TRACC-SELECT, Australian multi-site prospective registries. Clinicopathologic characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes were examined. Survival outcomes for 1L pembrolizumab-treated patients were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier. From 36 sites, 120 dMMR mCRC patients were identified; 109 (91%) received systemic treatment. 1L treatment included pembrolizumab (n = 103, 94%), clinical trial enrolment (n = 4, 4%), and chemotherapy (n = 2, 2%). Among pembrolizumab-treated patients, median age was 75 years, 49% had a BRAFV600E mutation, and 17% had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) ≥ 2. Median follow-up was 25.8 months. The real-world objective response rate was 58%, while 17% had progressive disease as best response. Median duration of therapy was 15.2 months. Of 74 patients who discontinued pembrolizumab, 21 (28%) completed the 2-year course, 28 (38%) discontinued due to progressive disease, 11 (15%) due to toxicity, 6 (8%) after achieving complete response before 2 years, and 8 (11%) for other reasons. Median PFS was 37.9 months. Median overall survival (OS) was not reached; 12- and 24-month OS rates were 88% and 77%, respectively. This real-world cohort included older patients with higher rates of BRAFV600E mutation and poorer ECOG PS than KEYNOTE-177. There has been rapid and wide uptake of pembrolizumab as a new standard of care, with promising outcomes. Ongoing data collection and analyses will evaluate predictors of immunotherapy response and real-world second-line treatment patterns and outcomes.

Oncological emergencies in radiology: Classic presentations and current challenges.
items.abstract: The number of oncology patients requiring emergency care continues to rise. Many of these emergencies are life-threatening and may result either from the underlying malignancy or the diagnostic and therapeutic procedures employed. In this context, imaging techniques play a fundamental role by enabling early detection and guiding clinical management. Among the most challenging scenarios are opportunistic infections in patients undergoing haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, where pulmonary involvement presents a significant diagnostic challenge. In addition to being familiar with complications related to conventional treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy, radiologists must also be able to recognise adverse effects associated with immunotherapy modalities, which can also require urgent consultations. This article provides an illustrative review of the main oncological emergencies, highlighting the radiologist's role in their identification.

Genetic Variants in TLR3, TLR7 and TLR8 Modulate COVID-19 Severity and Inflammatory Responses in a Moroccan Cohort.
items.abstract: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) 3, 7, and 8 are essential for antiviral immunity. TLR7 and TLR8, as X-linked genes, may contribute to sex-specific antiviral responses. This study investigated associations between TLR polymorphisms (TLR3 rs3775291, TLR7 rs179008, TLR7 rs3853839, and TLR8 rs3764880) and COVID-19 severity in 368 unvaccinated Moroccan patients (181 severe, 187 asymptomatic/moderate cases). SNP genotyping was performed using TaqMan predesigned assays. Complete blood counts and C-reactive protein levels were measured using automated platforms. Anti-nucleocapsid and anti-receptor-binding domain IgG antibodies were assessed by chemiluminescence immunoassay. In sex-stratified analyses of TLR7 rs3853839, increased risk in females was restricted to G/G carriers under recessive (OR = 4.68, 95% CI = 1.49-14.73, p = 0.0043) and codominant (OR = 4.65, 95% CI = 1.45-14.92, p = 0.017) models. TLR8 rs3764880 was associated with disease severity in both sexes: the G allele increased risk in males (OR = 2.79, 95% CI = 1.52-5.06, p = 0.0008), whereas the G/G genotype in females was associated with protection under a recessive (OR = 0.22, 95% CI = 0.09-0.58, p = 0.0015) and codominant model (OR = 0.80, 95% CI = 0.32-1.97, p = 0.0075). The A-A-C haplotype (OR = 2.99, 95% CI = 1.08-8.26, p = 0.036) of TLR7/TLR8 increased severity risk in females. The TLR7 rs179008 was associated with higher anti-RBD IgG levels in asymptomatic females (p = 0.025). These findings indicate that TLR genetic variation contributes to heterogeneity in COVID-19 outcomes and may inform risk stratification.

items.title: Whole genome sequencing and pathogenicity analysis of Fusarium arcuatisporum from peanut stems.
items.abstract: Fusarium arcuatisporum is a widely distributed filamentous plant pathogen. Here, we isolated and identified Fusarium arcuatisporum strain SLY02, sequenced its complete genome, and investigated its molecular pathogenic mechanisms. Strain SLY02 formed white powdery aerial hyphae on PDA medium, sharing 98% sequence identity with Fusarium arcuatisporum. Whole genome sequencing generated a 38.67 Mb genome encoding 7691 genes, including 1564 pathogen-host interaction genes, 409 virulence factors, 736 carbohydrate-active enzymes, and 65 genes distributed in 10 secondary metabolic clusters. In mouse infection models, 7-day infection significantly increased liver indices (P < 0.01). Histopathological staining revealed granulomatous hepatitis, neutrophil infiltration, hepatocellular necrosis, and black hyphae in liver nodules. Necroptosis-related genes (RIPK1, RIPK3, MLKL, TNF-α) were highly significantly upregulated (P < 0.01), while Caspase-8 was markedly downregulated (P < 0.01). Antifungal susceptibility testing showed strain SLY02 was sensitive to itraconazole but resistant to caspofungin, voriconazole, and amphotericin B. This study provides important genomic resources and in-depth mechanistic insights into the pathogenic mechanism of Fusarium arcuatisporum, offering a reference for preventing Fusarium contamination in feed and controlling related livestock diseases.

items.title: Discovery of two novel antioxidant peptides from Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) skin and exploration of their antioxidant mechanisms via network pharmacology.
items.abstract: Oxidative stress is a common pathogenic basis of chronic diseases. Although synthetic antioxidants are effective, safety concerns have increased interest in natural bioactive peptides because of their sustainable sourcing, biocompatibility, and safety. This study employed an integrated strategy-enzymatic hydrolysis, membrane separation, preparative high performance liquid chromatography (prep-HPLC), mass spectrometry identification, in silico screening, and in vitro validation-to discover novel antioxidant peptides from Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) skin and reveal their potential mechanisms via network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. By optimizing enzymatic hydrolysis and combining membrane separation with prep-HPLC, a highly active intermediate, R4, was isolated, achieving 1,1-diphenyl-2-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) and 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) free radical scavenging rates of 16.65% ± 0.21% and 92.1% ± 0.41% at 1.0 mg/mL, respectively. Mass spectrometry analysis and computational virtual screening identified two potent antioxidant peptides: GERGPPGPM and PGSGPGPGSGP, with half-maximal effective concentration (EC 50 ) values of 0.21 mg/mL and 0.28 mg/mL against ABTS, respectively, while maintaining activity retention rates above 90% following in vitro gastrointestinal digestion. Network pharmacology suggested these peptides may act via key targets including MMP9, CASP3, BCL2, JUN, and PTGS2, as well as pathways related to apoptosis, cancer, TNF signaling, and hepatitis B. Molecular docking and MD simulations further provided computational evidence for the possible interactions between the identified peptides and predicted core targets. This research provides a reproducible workflow for the high-value utilization of cod skin byproducts and offers theoretical and methodological support for developing natural peptide-based antioxidants for potential applications in functional foods and related fields.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Detection and Characterization of Colorectal Polyps during Colonoscopy: Evidence and Future Perspectives.
items.abstract: Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention because it enables early detection and removal of premalignant lesions. However, lesions can still be missed, and endoscopic differentiation of neoplastic from nonneoplastic polyps remains variable, particularly for diminutive lesions. The potential of artificial intelligence (AI) as a supportive technology for improving both polyp detection and characterization during colonoscopy has therefore been investigated. Since early studies of convolutional neural network-based computer-aided detection (CADe), the focus has shifted from retrospective image-based validation to real-time randomized trials, meta-analyses, and clinical guideline discussions. Accumulating evidence suggests that CADe improves surrogate detection outcomes, including the adenoma detection rate (ADR), polyp detection rate, adenomas per colonoscopy, and adenoma miss rate. Although a higher ADR is associated with a lower risk of postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer, it remains unknown whether the incremental improvement in the ADR achieved by CADe translates into lower postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer incidence or colorectal cancer-related mortality. Recent multicenter data further support the effectiveness of real-time CADe systems in improving detection-related outcomes, while also indicating that benefit varies with lesion characteristics and user experience. In parallel, computer-aided diagnosis (CADx) has been developed to assist the optical characterization of colorectal polyps, particularly for diminutive lesions and potential resect-and-discard or diagnose-and-leave strategies. CADx systems using white-light imaging and structured high-confidence diagnostic rules show promise, but the clinical implementation of CADx remains less mature than that of CADe. This review summarizes current evidence for AI-assisted polyp detection and characterization and discusses limitations and future directions for integrating CADe and CADx into human-centered colonoscopy practices.

items.title: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor as a Radiotheranostic Target in Orthotopic Models of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a 5-y survival rate of approximately 20%. Although glypican-3-targeted radiotheranostics are under development, a plurality of patients with HCC lack glypican-3 expression, underscoring the need for alternative targetable antigens. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is overexpressed in 50%-70% of HCC tumors and represents a clinically validated therapeutic target. Here, we developed and evaluated a panitumumab-based EGFR-targeted radiotheranostic pair, [ 89 Zr]Zr-desferrioxamine-panitumumab ([ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani) for immuno-PET and [ 225 Ac]Ac-Macropa-panitumumab ([ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani) for targeted α-particle therapy, in clinically relevant orthotopic HCC models. Methods: Panitumumab was conjugated with desferrioxamine or Macropa chelators and radiolabeled with 89 Zr or 225 Ac, respectively. EGFR expression was characterized across a panel of HCC cell lines. Binding affinity, biodistribution, and tumor specificity were assessed in subcutaneous and orthotopic Huh-7 models, with EGFR-mediated targeting confirmed by blocking (200-fold molar excess of unlabeled panitumumab). Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in mice bearing orthotopic Huh-7-Luc + tumors ( n = 6 per group) after a single 9.3 kBq dose of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani, with longitudinal monitoring by bioluminescence imaging, [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani immuno-PET, and blood chemistry. Results: [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani exhibited high-affinity binding to EGFR (dissociation constant, 0.35 nM) and demonstrated robust tumor accumulation in both subcutaneous Huh-7 (20.6 ± 2.6 %IA/g) and orthotopic Huh-7-Luc + tumors (19.3 ± 2.0 %IA/g) at 120-192 h postinjection. Biodistribution of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani closely mirrored that of [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani across organs and tumors, with tumor uptake reduced approximately 5-fold by blocking (21.7 ± 1.1 vs. 4.5 ± 0.6 %IA/g; P 225 Ac]Ac-Pani induced substantial early tumor regression and significantly prolonged median survival (70 d) compared with vehicle (28 d) and blocking (35 d) groups (log-rank P Conclusion: [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani and [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani represent a radiotheranostic pair that enables EGFR-specific imaging and targeted α-particle therapy in orthotopic HCC models. These findings establish EGFR as a promising radiotheranostic target in HCC, broadening the patient population eligible for image-guided radiopharmaceutical interventions for liver cancer.

items.title: What do we know about pseudocirrhosis? The role of the radiologist.
items.abstract: Pseudocirrhosis is a radiological diagnosis characterised by liver morphological alterations simulating cirrhosis in oncological patients, despite the absence of histopathological features of true cirrhosis. which relies almost entirely on imaging findings, carries important prognostic implications, as it is associated with increased morbidity and mortality, and a heightened risk of developing encephalopathy, oesophageal/gastric variceal bleeding, or hepatic failure. Nevertheless, despite its clinical relevance, many questions remain regarding its pathophysiology, predisposing factors, and optimal management. In oncology patients with hepatic metastases, the presence of morphostructural liver changes such as surface retraction and nodularity, parenchymal atrophy, and/or hypertrophy of the caudate lobe should raise suspicion in the radiologist. This update aims to present current knowledge and the clinical relevance of this entity, highlighting its main clinical and imaging features.

items.title: Association between preoperative multidisciplinary team discussion and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases undergoing initial hepatic resection: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Evidence regarding the association between multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) undergoing hepatic resection remains limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative MDT discussion and survival outcomes in this surgically treated population. We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed CRLM who underwent initial hepatic resection at our center between September 2020 and December 2024. Patients were categorized into MDT and non-MDT groups based on whether a preoperative MDT discussion was conducted. To improve balance in observed baseline characteristics, 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed. Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint, and recurrence-free survival (RFS) was analyzed as a secondary endpoint. Survival curves were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared with the log-rank test. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation (MI), and univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to assess the association between MDT discussion and survival outcomes. Sensitivity analyses using complete-case multivariable Cox regression, Cox regression in the propensity score-matched cohort, and average treatment effect among the treated (ATT) weighting were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. A total of 256 patients were included, including 79 in the MDT group and 177 in the non-MDT group. After 1:1 PSM, 72 matched pairs were identified. Before PSM, the MDT group had significantly better OS than the non-MDT group (P=0.03). The 1- and 3-year OS rates were 97.2% and 77.9% in the MDT group, compared with 88.8% and 57.5% in the non-MDT group, respectively. After PSM, the difference in OS remained significant (P=0.01), with corresponding 1- and 3-year OS rates of 98.5% and 77.9% versus 85.3% and 49.1%, respectively. No significant difference in RFS was observed before (P=0.52) or after PSM (P=0.16). In MI-pooled univariable Cox regression analysis, MDT discussion was associated with improved OS [hazard ratio (HR): 0.541; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.301-0.975; P=0.04], and this association remained significant in multivariable analysis (HR: 0.483; 95% CI: 0.260-0.897; P=0.02). MDT discussion was not independently associated with RFS in multivariable analysis (HR: 0.928; 95% CI: 0.654-1.317; P=0.67). Sensitivity analyses using complete-case multivariable Cox regression, Cox regression in the propensity score-matched cohort, and ATT weighting yielded generally consistent results with the primary analysis. Preoperative MDT discussion was associated with improved OS but not RFS in patients with CRLM undergoing initial hepatic resection. These findings support the potential value of MDT discussion in preoperative decision-making for this patient population.
